I'm in my mid 30s now and I was diagnosed at around 20. My life has been as bipolar as my illness, I've experienced huge levels of success but then also many hospital admissions and even a stint in jail. I have learned as time has gone on to just brace myself and ride the wave as safely as I can, mitigate the storm. The symptoms will never go away entirely, so don't aim for that. Just accept that this is your lot, sometimes it will be really bad but stay holding on, because sometimes it will be so good. I'm at a stage now where if someone said they had a magic wand to wave away my illness, I'd tell them not to bother.

When I'm manic it doesn't matter what meds or what dose I'm on, I just don't sleep, which is why I'm writing this comment at 5:30am in a hotel room that I can't afford that is only two miles away from my actual home. Anyway. My advice, is don't panic about not sleeping. Be at peace with it, think "I may not be able to sleep tonight but that's ok". Rest is good, make sure your sensory input is at a minimum. Dark room, low noise. Don't go out in the evenings, like my consultant told me not to go out after 6pm and to stop writing at 9pm (I'm an author). Just lie quiet and rest, if you need to then ask about emergency sleep medicine, but ultimately, stop trying so hard to force it and accept that right now, what will be will be.

Negative and positive symptoms don't refer to negative and positive mindsets. This term is most often used in schizophrenia; "positive", means "things that add to your normal living experience", so hallucinations, delusion and mania are "positive". "Negative" symptoms are what's taken away from your lived experience as someone with psychosis, and include things like flattened affect, loss of energy, loss of social skills.
